newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - Busang impact on investors to linger.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Busang impact on investors to linger.

text.p: The impact of the Busang gold mine debacle will be felt for years and will prompt investors to be more cautious in acquiring mining companies with unproven reserves, a Canadian lawyer said on Thursday.

"Investors will be asking a lot more questions," Steven Trumper, managing partner of the Hong Kong office of Osler, Hoskin & Harcourt, one of the largest law firms in Canada, told Reuters in an interview at a mining conference in Singapore.

"I think what Bre-X has done a great deal is to educate investors into the finer points of the correct way in which mine projects need to be analysed," said Trumper, who is familiar with mining issues.
This would mean tighter reporting of results by exploration companies with some requiring independent verification of mineral resource and ore reserve estimates, he said.
Trumper said in a report made available on Thursday that "repercussions from the Bre-X affair will be felt for many years to come in the context of due diligence for mining projects".
Shares of Bre-X Minerals Ltd collapsed in Toronto after the report by independent auditors Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd that there was no viable gold deposit in Busang.

"It is also likely that mining companies and their financiers will be much more cautious with unproven resources or reserves. Prudent bidders are likely to insist that any transaction be made conditional on satisfactory verification drilling, sample preparation and assay results," Trumper said.

The controversy may also prompt governments in Asia to implement "more restrictive policies" on mining "as national governments seek to avoid future embarrassment and take more control over their mineral riches," he added.
